correctness.rationale: For each horizon T and vertex v let a_v count its excited events. Two consecutive excitations at a vertex are separated by ≥3 time steps. Along any edge every adjacent-time transmission uses distinct endpoint excitation events; otherwise same vertex would be excited at times distance two. Hence transmissions per edge ≤min(a_u,a_v), whereas each noninitial excitation requires q incoming transmissions. The layer-cake sum Σ_edges min(a_u,a_v)=Σ_{j≥1}|E[S_j]|≤ρ(G) Σ_v a_v gives (q−ρ)N_T≤qm. If ρ<q finite excitation budget forces extinction and initial refractory states clear by N+1. For K_{2q,2q}, ρ=q and explicit four-class state cycle is primitive period 4. Independent exhaustive graph/state enumeration checked all 216+5184+248589 initial states on all simple labeled graphs of size 3,4,5 with ρ<2, for q=2, including event budget and clock bound, independently of packaged verify_density.py. This finite check is corroboration, not the all-graph proof.
